name: Leidos
description: Leidos is a services and systems contractor: it runs IT and cyber for the intelligence community and defense, manages health systems for the VA and military health (managed health services), operates airport security screening and border technology, and builds defense systems such as unmanned vessels and sensors. Government work is the bulk of revenue (49 percent from the Department of War and the Intelligence Community in 2025). It is paid mostly on cost-plus, time-and-materials and fixed-price contracts, so margins are single-digit except health. Backlog was $49.0 billion at the start of fiscal 2026. A 2026 reorganisation replaced the segments and added the $2.4 billion Entrust acquisition (utility engineering).

gics.note: Conventional label per Wikipedia's List of S&P 500 companies (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_S%26P_500_companies, read 2026-10-01), which gives only the sector and the sub-industry; GICS industry group and industry are not shown there so are left null. Mowgli classification is not set here.

employees.note: About 47,000 full and part-time employees, about 41,900 in the US. FY2025 10-K

businessLines.name: National Security & Digital
businessLines.how: Agencies pay for staffed engineering and IT services (cost-plus, time-and-materials, fixed-price) on multi-year contracts; revenue follows headcount and program awards.
businessLines.description: IT modernisation, cyber, mission software and digital services for defense, intelligence and civil national-security customers (FY2025 segment structure).

businessLines.name: Health & Civil
businessLines.how: Federal agencies pay for medical examinations and managed-health programs, for software and systems integration, and for air traffic systems; write-ups on managed health services programs help lift margin to 23.7 percent versus about 10 percent in national security IT.
businessLines.description: Managed health services (clinics and medical disability and behavioral exams for the VA), health mission software (one electronic health record for DoW and VA), air traffic control systems for the FAA and other air navigation providers, energy and environment work for the DoE, and life-sciences R&D (FY2025 structure).

businessLines.name: Commercial & International
businessLines.how: Customers such as TSA, CBP, airports, utilities and UK/Australian agencies pay for security equipment when delivered plus service contracts, and for utility modernisation project work.
businessLines.description: Security detection products (people scanners, CT carry-on and checked baggage scanners, explosive trace detectors; 30,000+ units in 120+ countries; primary supplier of cargo and vehicle inspection systems to US CBP), energy infrastructure work for investor-owned utilities, and UK and Australian government services (FY2025 structure).

businessLines.name: Defense Systems
businessLines.how: The Department of War pays under development and production contracts for platforms and systems; revenue follows program volume.
businessLines.description: Advanced space, aerial, surface and sub-surface manned and unmanned defense systems: manufacturing, prototyping, weapons development (FY2025 structure).

brands.name: Entrust (acquired 2026-03-27)
brands.note: Engineering firm doing infrastructure design, grid modernisation and program management for electric, gas and pipeline utilities; $2.4B cash purchase price; added $371M of backlog (Q2 2026 10-Q)

brands.name: Kudu Dynamics
brands.note: Acquired in fiscal 2025; $60M of FY2025 segment revenue
